sec: 7.5 Updating Records in a Text File

cards.t: Why read data from text files?
cards.tz: 为什么从文本文件读取数据
cards.en:
Intuition: imagine typing 200 exam marks every time you test your program. One typo and you start again. A text file (a file holding plain characters, e.g. .txt, .csv, .json) keeps the data so you type it once.

Rule: when a program has a large number of inputs or outputs, read from / write to a text file instead of using input()/print().

  • Data is stored outside the program, so it is kept after the program ends.
  • It can be reused and edited (like a simple database).
  • GIGO (Garbage In, Garbage Out): bad input data gives bad results, so we preprocess and parse text (remove extra spaces, special characters) first. This matters in machine learning, where text files are training data.

Exam wording: “Data in a text file can be reused and does not need to be re-entered each time the program runs.” “Data is kept permanently after the program ends.”
cards.zh:
直觉：每次测试程序都要输入 200 个分数，打错一个就要重来。文本文件（text file）（只存纯字符的文件，如 .txt、.csv、.json）可以把数据存起来，只输入一次。

规则：程序有大量输入或输出时，用文本文件代替 input()/print()。

  • 数据存在程序之外，程序结束后仍然保留。
  • 可重复使用和修改，像一个简单数据库（simple database）。
  • GIGO（Garbage In, Garbage Out）：输入差，结果也差，所以先预处理和解析（preprocess and parse），例如删多余空格和特殊字符。机器学习常用文本作训练数据。

考试写法：“Data in a text file can be reused and does not need to be re-entered each time the program runs.”

ex.q: Give TWO advantages of reading 200 marks from a text file instead of input().
ex.a:
1. The marks are typed once and reused every run.
2. If one mark is wrong, only that line is edited, not all 200 re-entered.
(Also: data is kept after the program ends.)
ex.az: 1. 只输入一次，可重复使用。2. 打错只改那一行。

ex.q: A program reads tweets from tweets.txt to train a model. Some lines have extra spaces and emojis. What should be done first, and why?
ex.a:
1. Preprocess the text: remove extra spaces and special characters.
2. Reason: GIGO, dirty input gives poor results.
ex.az: 先预处理（删空格、特殊字符），因为 GIGO。

ex.q: A student says: “Variables already store data, so text files are useless.” What is wrong?
ex.a: Variables are stored in RAM and are lost when the program ends. A text file is stored on disk, so the data stays and can be reused. That is the reason to use files.
ex.az: 变量在内存，程序结束就消失；文件存在磁盘，会保留。

marks = []
f = open("marks.txt", "w")
f.write("67\n82\n45")
f.close()
f = open("marks.txt", "r")
for line in f.readlines():
    marks.append(int(line))
f.close()
print(marks, sum(marks))

cards.t: Opening a file: open()
cards.en:
Intuition: before you read a book you open it. open() “opens” a file and gives you a handle to it.

Rule: f = open("datafile.txt", "r")

  • Parameter 1: file name with extension.
  • Parameter 2: mode ("r", "w", "a", "x").
  • It returns a file object (the handle). Store it in a variable (here f), then use f.read(), f.write(), f.close().
  • If the file is not in the same folder as the program, give the complete path, e.g. "D:/data/datafile.txt".

Exam wording: “open() takes two parameters, the file name and the mode, and returns a file object.”
cards.zh:
直觉：看书前先打开书。open() 打开文件，给你一个“把手”。

规则：f = open("datafile.txt", "r")

  • 参数 1：文件名（连扩展名）。
  • 参数 2：模式（mode）（"r"、"w"、"a"、"x"）。
  • 返回文件对象（file object），存入变量 f，之后用 f.read()、f.write()、f.close()。
  • 文件和程序不在同一文件夹时要写完整路径（complete path）。

考试写法：“open() takes two parameters, the file name and the mode, and returns a file object.”

ex.q: Write a statement that opens scores.txt for reading and stores the file object in data.
ex.a:
data = open("scores.txt", "r")
1. First argument: file name with extension.
2. Second argument: mode "r".
ex.az: 第一个参数是文件名，第二个是模式 "r"。

ex.q: The file report.txt is in folder D:/ict/, but the program is in C:/code/. How do you open it?
ex.a:
Give the complete path: 
f = open("D:/ict/report.txt", "r")
ex.az: 不在同一文件夹，要写完整路径。

ex.q: What is wrong with open("scores", "r").read() when the file is called scores.txt?
ex.a: The name must include the extension. "scores" is a different (missing) file, so you get FileNotFoundError. Write "scores.txt".
ex.az: 漏了扩展名 .txt，会找不到文件。

f = open("datafile.txt", "w")

f = open("datafile.txt", "r")
print(type(f).__name__)
print(f.read())
f.close()

cards.t: The four file modes: r, x, w, a
cards.en:
Intuition: the mode tells Python what you plan to do: look (r), make new (x), rewrite (w) or add more (a).

ModeMeaningFile missingFile exists
"r"readerrorread it
"x"createcreatederror
"w"write, overwritecreatedold content erased
"a"write, appendcreatedadded at end
  • Only "r" fails on a missing file; only "x" fails on an existing file.
  • A file opened with "r" cannot be written; one opened with "w"/"a"/"x" cannot be read.

Exam wording: “Mode w overwrites the original content; mode a appends new content to the end of the file.”
cards.zh:
直觉：模式告诉 Python 你想做什么：看（r）、新建（x）、重写（w）、加内容（a）。

模式意思文件不存在文件已存在
"r"读取出错读取
"x"创建创建出错
"w"写入，覆盖创建旧内容被清除
"a"写入，附加创建加到末尾
  • 只有 "r" 怕文件不存在，只有 "x" 怕文件已存在。
  • "r" 打开的文件不能写；"w"/"a"/"x" 打开的不能读。

考试写法：“Mode w overwrites the original content; mode a appends new content to the end of the file.”

ex.q: log.txt contains "Day 1". Give the content after: (i) "w" then write "Day 2"; (ii) "a" then write "Day 2"; (iii) open with "x".
ex.a:
(i) overwrite → Day 2
(ii) append → Day 1Day 2 (no automatic new line)
(iii) FileExistsError, the file already exists.

ex.q: Which mode should a program use to keep a running history of logins without losing old ones?
ex.a: "a". 1. Old lines stay. 2. Each new login is added at the end. 3. If the file is missing, it is created.
ex.az: 用 "a"，旧记录保留，新记录加到末尾。

ex.q: A student opens results.txt with "w" to read the old results first, then add one more. What goes wrong?
ex.a: Opening with "w" erases the content immediately, and a "w" file cannot be read (io.UnsupportedOperation). Correct: open with "r" to read, close, then open with "a" to add.
ex.az: "w" 一打开就清空内容，而且不能读。应先 "r" 读，再 "a" 加。

f = open("log.txt", "w")
f.write("Day 1")
f.close()
f = open("log.txt", "a")
f.write("Day 2")
f.close()
print(open("log.txt", "r").read())
f = open("log.txt", "x")

cards.t: Closing a file: close()
cards.en:
Intuition: closing a file is like pressing “Save and exit”. Until then, written text may still be waiting in memory (a buffer, a temporary holding area).

Rule: after finishing, call f.close().

  • It saves the written content to disk and releases the file for other programs.
  • Brackets matter: f.close without () does not call the function.
  • Pattern: open → read/write → close.

Exam wording: “Close the file after the file operations so that the content is saved.”
cards.zh:
直觉：关闭文件就像“保存并退出”。之前写入的文字可能还在内存的缓冲区（buffer）里。

规则：完成后调用 f.close()。

  • 把内容存到磁盘，并释放文件。
  • 括号不能漏：f.close 没有 () 不会调用函数。
  • 流程：open → read/write → close。

考试写法：“Close the file after the file operations so that the content is saved.”

ex.q: Complete the program so it writes "Hi" into a.txt and closes it.
ex.a:
f = open("a.txt", "w")
f.write("Hi")
f.close()

ex.q: Give TWO reasons to close a file.
ex.a:
1. Written content is saved to disk.
2. The file is released so other programs (or a later open) can use it.
ex.az: 1. 保存内容；2. 释放文件。

ex.q: A program ends with f.close. The output file is sometimes empty. Why?
ex.a: f.close only refers to the method; without () it is never called, so buffered data may not be written. Write f.close().
ex.az: 没有括号就没有调用，内容可能没写入。

code.src:
f = open("a.txt", "w")
f.write("Hi")
f.close()
print(f.closed)
print(open("a.txt").read())

notes.t: Write text (may wait in a buffer)
notes.tz: 写入（可能暂存在缓冲区）

notes.t: Flush to disk and release the file
True: the file is now closed

cards.t: Checking whether a file exists: os.path.exists()
cards.tz: 用 os.path.exists() 检查文件是否存在
cards.en:
Intuition: knock before you enter. Opening a missing file with "r" crashes the program (a run-time error, an error that happens while running).

Rule:

  • import os first.
  • os.path.exists("targetfile.txt") returns a Boolean: True if the file exists, else False.
  • Put it in an if: open only when True, otherwise show a message.

Exam wording: “Check whether the file exists with os.path.exists() before opening it, to avoid a run-time error.”
cards.zh:
直觉：进门前先敲门。用 "r" 打开不存在的文件会令程序崩溃（运行时错误 run-time error）。

规则：

  • 先 import os。
  • os.path.exists("targetfile.txt") 返回布尔值：存在为 True，否则 False。
  • 放在 if 里：True 才打开，否则显示信息。

考试写法：“Check whether the file exists with os.path.exists() before opening it, to avoid a run-time error.”

ex.q: Write code that prints notes.txt if it exists, otherwise prints "No file".
ex.a:
import os
if os.path.exists("notes.txt"):
    f = open("notes.txt", "r")
    print(f.read())
    f.close()
else:
    print("No file")
ex.az: 先 import os，再用 if 判断。

ex.q: What type of value does os.path.exists() return? Give both possible values.
ex.a: A Boolean: True (exists) or False (does not exist).

ex.q: A student writes if os.path.exists("a.txt"): ... but gets NameError: name 'os' is not defined. Fix it.
ex.a: The os library was not imported. Add import os at the top of the program.

code.src:
import os
print(os.path.exists("notes.txt"))
open("notes.txt", "w").close()
if os.path.exists("notes.txt"):
    f = open("notes.txt", "r")
    print("Lines:", len(f.readlines()))
    f.close()
else:
    print("No file")

notes.tz: 现在为 True，可安全打开

notes.t: Friendly message instead of a crash

cards.t: read(): whole file as one string
cards.tz: read()：读取全部内容为字符串
cards.en:
Intuition: read() swallows the whole file in one bite and gives it back as one long string.

Rule: content = f.read()

  • Reads all content until EOF (end of file) and returns one string (str).
  • The between lines is kept inside the string.
  • Empty file, or pointer already at the end → returns "".
  • Useful to count characters, search, or content.split(" ") to get lines without .

Exam wording: “read() reads all the content in the file and returns it as a string.”
cards.zh:
直觉：read() 一口吞下整个文件，返回一个长字符串。

规则：content = f.read()

  • 读全部内容直到 EOF，返回一个字符串。
  • 行之间的 保留在字符串中。
  • 文件为空或指针已到末尾 → 返回 ""。
  • 适合数字符、搜索，或用 content.split(" ") 得到不含 的各行。

考试写法：“read() reads all the content in the file and returns it as a string.”

ex.q: input.txt has 3 lines A, B, C. What does print(repr(f.read())) show?
ex.a: 'A B C'. 1. kept between lines. 2. No after the last line.

ex.q: Using read(), write code to count the lines of input.txt.
ex.a:
f = open("input.txt", "r")
print(len(f.read().split("\n")))
f.close()
For A, B, C this prints 3.

ex.q: A student calls print(f.read()) twice. The second prints a blank line. Why?
ex.a: After the first read() the pointer is at EOF, so the second read() returns "". Store the result in a variable once and reuse it.
ex.az: 第一次已读到 EOF，第二次返回空字符串。应存进变量。

code.src:
f = open("testfile.txt", "w")
f.write("This is line one.\nThis is line two.\nThis is line three.")
f.close()
f = open("testfile.txt", "r")
content = f.read()
f.close()
print(type(content))

print(len(content.split("\n")))

cards.t: readline(): one line at a time
cards.en:
Intuition: like reading a list with your finger, one line, then the next line.

Rule: line = f.readline()

  • Reads one line (the first line on the first call) and returns it as a string.
  • Stops after a \n (the \n is included) or at EOF.
  • Each call continues from where the last one stopped.
  • At EOF it returns the empty string "", which is how a loop knows to stop.

Exam wording: “readline() reads one line of the file and returns it as a string; it returns an empty string when the end of file is reached.”
cards.zh:
直觉：像用手指一行一行地读名单。

规则：line = f.readline()

  • 读一行（第一次读第一行），返回字符串。
  • 读到 \n（返回值包含 \n）或 EOF 为止。
  • 每次从上次停下的地方继续。
  • 到 EOF 返回空字符串 ""，循环靠它停止。

考试写法：“readline() reads one line of the file and returns it as a string; it returns an empty string when the end of file is reached.”

ex.q: A file contains "Hello\nWorld". Give a, b, c after three readline() calls.
ex.a:
a = "Hello\n" (with \n)
b = "World" (last line)
c = "" (EOF)
ex.az: a 含 \n；b 无；c 空字符串。

ex.q: What is len(a) for a = "Hello\n"?
ex.a: H-e-l-l-o is 5, plus \n is 1 → 6.

ex.q: A student prints each line with print(f.readline()) and sees an extra blank line after each one. Why, and how to fix?
ex.a: The line already ends with \n and print() adds another. Fix: print(line.replace("\n", "")) or print(line, end="").
ex.az: 行尾已有 \n，print 又加一个。去掉 \n 或用 end=""。

f.close()
f = open("hw.txt", "r")
a = f.readline()
b = f.readline()
c = f.readline()
f.close()
print(repr(a), repr(b), repr(c))

cards.t: readlines(): list of lines
cards.en:
Intuition: readlines() cuts the file into strips, one per line, and puts them in a list.

Rule: lines = f.readlines()

  • Reads all content; each line is one list item; returns a list.
  • Every item except usually the last ends with \n.
  • len(lines) = number of lines.
  • Clean items with replace("\n", "") before using them.

Exam wording: “readlines() reads all the content and returns a list, with each line as a list item.”
cards.zh:
直觉：readlines() 把文件按行剪成一条条，放进列表。

规则：lines = f.readlines()

  • 读全部内容，每行一项，返回 list。
  • 除最后一项外，通常都以 \n 结尾。
  • len(lines) = 行数。
  • 先用 replace("\n", "") 清理。

考试写法：“readlines() reads all the content and returns a list, with each line as a list item.”

ex.q: text.txt has one line "Today is Monday.". How many items does readlines() return? What is item 0?
ex.a: 1 item: "Today is Monday." (no \n, it is the last line).

ex.q: Write code to print the last line of data.txt using readlines().
ex.a:
f = open("data.txt", "r")
lines = f.readlines()
f.close()
print(lines[len(lines)-1])
ex.az: 用索引 len-1 取最后一项。

ex.q: A student compares lines[0] == "Rose" where the first line is Rose, but gets False. Why?
ex.a: lines[0] is "Rose "; the hidden makes it different. Compare lines[0].replace(" ", "") == "Rose".

cards.t: Comparing read(), readline(), readlines()
cards.en:
Intuition: all three read the same file; they differ in how much they read and what type they return.

FunctionReadsReturnsUse when
read()all, to EOFone stringwhole text: count, search, split
readline()one lineone string (with \n)while loop, line by line, stop early
readlines()alllist of stringsfor loop, indexing lines

All three move the hidden pointer, so after read() or readlines() a further read gives nothing.

Exam wording: “read() returns a string of the whole file, readline() returns one line as a string, and readlines() returns a list of all lines.”
cards.zh:
直觉：三者读同一个文件，分别在读多少和返回什么类型。

函数读取返回适用
read()全部一个字符串整体处理
readline()一行一个字符串（含 \n）while 循环逐行
readlines()全部列表for 循环、索引

三者都会移动隐藏指针，读完全部后再读就没有内容。

考试写法：“read() returns a string of the whole file, readline() returns one line as a string, and readlines() returns a list of all lines.”

ex.q: Which function gives a list? Which gives one line?
ex.a: readlines() gives a list; readline() gives one line.
ex.az: readlines() 给列表；readline() 给一行。

ex.q: A file is 2 GB. Which function is safest to process it line by line, and why?
ex.a: readline() in a while loop: only one line is in memory at a time, and you can stop early.

ex.q: A program calls f.read() then f.readlines() on the same file and expects a list of lines. What does it get?
ex.a: An empty list []. read() already moved the pointer to EOF. Reopen the file, or split the read() string.
ex.az: 得到 []，因为指针已在 EOF。

cards.t: Text file streaming and the hidden pointer
cards.tz: 文本文件串流与隐藏指针
cards.en:
Intuition: think of a cassette tape. The play head only moves forward. Python reads a file the same way.

Rule:

  • The content is a stream: one continuous row of characters.
  • On open, a hidden pointer sits at the first character.
  • Each read moves the pointer forward past what it read.
  • The next read starts where the pointer stopped, not from the start.
  • To read from the start again, close and reopen the file.

Exam wording: “When a file is opened, a hidden pointer points to the first character; each read operation starts from the position where the pointer last stopped.”
cards.zh:
直觉：像录音带，磁头只会向前走。Python 读文件也一样。

规则：

  • 内容是一个串流（stream）：连续的一串字符。
  • 打开时，隐藏指针（hidden pointer）在第一个字符。
  • 每次读取，指针向前移过读到的字符。
  • 下次从指针停下的位置开始。
  • 要从头再读，关闭再重新打开。

考试写法：“When a file is opened, a hidden pointer points to the first character; each read operation starts from the position where the pointer last stopped.”

ex.q: A file contains "abc\ndef". After line = f.readline(), what does f.read() return?
ex.a:
1. readline() reads "abc\n"; pointer stops at 'd'.
2. read() continues → "def".

ex.q: A file contains "12345". After f.read(2) (read 2 characters), what does f.read() return?
ex.a: read(2) moves the pointer past "12". read() returns "345".

ex.q: A student reads the file once to count lines, then loops readline() to print them, but nothing prints. Fix?
ex.a: The pointer is already at EOF. Close the file and open it again before the second pass (or keep the lines in a list).
ex.az: 指针已在 EOF，要重新打开。

frames.en: After open() the pointer is at the first character a.
frames.zh: 打开后指针在第一个字符 a。

frames.en: readline() reads a b c \n and returns "abc\n". Pointer now at d.
frames.zh: readline() 读 a b c \n，返回 "abc\n"，指针到 d。

frames.en: read() continues from d to EOF and returns "def".
frames.zh: read() 从 d 读到 EOF，返回 "def"。

frames.en: Pointer at EOF: any further read returns "" (or [] for readlines()).
frames.zh: 指针在 EOF：再读只得 ""（readlines() 得 []）。

cards.t: Special characters: Line Feed (LF) and End Of File (EOF)
cards.tz: 特殊字符 LF 与 EOF
cards.en:
Intuition: a text file has invisible marks, like “go to next line” and “the end”. You don't see them in Notepad, but they are stored.

  • Line Feed (LF), written : stored at the end of every line (normally not after the last line).
  • End Of File (EOF): marks the end of the text file.
  • read() reads until EOF. readline() reads until or EOF.
  • is one character: len("ab ") = 3.

Exam wording: “The line feed character is stored at the end of every line, and EOF is stored at the end of the text file.”
cards.zh:
直觉：文本文件里有看不见的记号，例如“换行”和“结束”。记事本不显示，但确实存在。

  • 换行 Line Feed (LF)，写作 ：存在每行末尾（最后一行通常没有）。
  • 檔尾 End Of File (EOF)：标示文件结束。
  • read() 读到 EOF；readline() 读到 或 EOF。
  • 是一个字符：len("ab ") = 3。

考试写法：“The line feed character is stored at the end of every line, and EOF is stored at the end of the text file.”

ex.q: readlines() returns ['Cat\n', 'Dog']. Give len() of each item.
A file has 5 lines and no \n after the last line. How many \n characters does it contain?
ex.a: One between each pair of lines: 5 − 1 = 4.

ex.q: A student says len("ab\n") is 4 because \n is two characters. Correct this.
ex.a: \n is written with 2 symbols but is one character (LF). The answer is 3.

code.src:
s = "Cat\nDog"
print(len(s))
print(s)
print(repr(s))
print(s.count("\n") + 1)

notes.t: \n is shown as a line break

demo.src:
s = "Cat\nDog"
print(len(s))
print(s)
print(repr(s))
print(s.count("\n") + 1)

cards.t: Tracing consecutive readline() calls
cards.en:
Intuition: each readline() is one step of your finger down the page.

For testfile.txt with 3 lines:

  1. On open, the pointer is at the first character.
  2. Call 1 reads until the pointer moves to the character after \n.
  3. Call 2 starts where the pointer stopped.
  4. Call 3 finds no \n before EOF, so it stops at the end.
  5. Call 4: pointer at EOF → empty string.

Exam wording: “The pointer has reached the end of file, so readline() returns an empty string.”
cards.zh:
直觉：每次 readline() 就是手指往下移一行。

testfile.txt 有 3 行：

  1. 打开时指针在第一个字符。
  2. 第 1 次读到指针移到 \n 后面的字符。
  3. 第 2 次从停下处开始。
  4. 第 3 次在 EOF 前找不到 \n，读到末尾就停。
  5. 第 4 次：指针在 EOF → 空字符串。

考试写法：“The pointer has reached the end of file, so readline() returns an empty string.”

ex.q: A file has 2 lines. On which call does readline() first return ""?
ex.a: Call 1 → line 1, call 2 → line 2, call 3 → "".

ex.q: A file has lines "X", "" (blank), "Y". Give the 4 results of readline().
ex.a: 1. "X " 2. " " (blank line still has ) 3. "Y" 4. ""

ex.q: A student thinks a blank line in the middle returns "" and stops the loop. Is that right?
ex.a: No. A blank line is "\n" (length 1). Only EOF gives "" (length 0).
ex.az: 不对，空行是 "\n"，只有 EOF 才是 ""。

code.src:
f = open("testfile.txt", "w")
f.write("This is line one.\nThis is line two.\nThis is line three.")
f.close()
f = open("testfile.txt", "r")
line1 = f.readline()
line2 = f.readline()
line3 = f.readline()
line4 = f.readline()
f.close()
print([line1, line2, line3, line4])

notes.tz: 创建示例文件（"w" 模式）
写入 3 行，用 \n 分隔

notes.t: Close it so the content is saved
notes.tz: 关闭文件，内容才会保存

code.out: ['This is line one.\n', 'This is line two.\n', 'This is line three.', '']

demo.src:

line2 = f.readline()
line3 = f.readline()
line4 = f.readline()

cards.t: Example 7.1: reading all lines with a readline() loop
cards.tz: 例题 7.1：用 readline() 循环读全部行
cards.en:
Intuition: keep reading lines until you get nothing back.

Pattern:

  1. Read one line before the loop.
  2. Loop while len(name) > 0 (or name != "").
  3. Inside: use the line, then read the next line at the end.

The result equals readlines(): items keep \n. A blank middle line is "\n" (length 1), so it does not stop the loop.

Exam wording: “If readline() returns an empty string, the pointer has reached the end of file, so the loop stops.”
cards.zh:
直觉：一直读，读到什么都没有就停。

模式：

  1. 循环前先读一行。
  2. while len(name) > 0（或 name != ""）。
  3. 循环内先使用这行，最后再读下一行。

结果与 readlines() 相同，各项含 \n。中间的空行是 "\n"（长度 1），不会令循环停止。

考试写法：“If readline() returns an empty string, the pointer has reached the end of file, so the loop stops.”

ex.q: Rewrite the loop condition without len().
ex.a: while name != "": — the same meaning: stop at EOF.

ex.q: Modify Example 7.1 so the names are stored without \n.
ex.a:
Change the add line to 
member = member + [name.replace("\n", "")]
Result: ['Zoe', 'Wendy', 'King'].
ex.az: 加入前先 replace 去掉 \n。

ex.q: A student forgets name = f.readline() inside the loop. What happens?
ex.a: name never changes, so len(name) > 0 stays True: an infinite loop adding "Zoe\n" forever. The next readline() must be the last statement in the loop.
ex.az: name 不变 → 无限循环。

code.src:
f = open("NewMember.txt", "w")
f.write("Zoe\nWendy\nKing")
f.close()
def newMemberList():
    member = []
    f = open("NewMember.txt", "r")
    name = f.readline()
    while len(name) > 0:
        member = member + [name]
        name = f.readline()
    f.close()
    return member
print(newMemberList())

notes.t: Read the first line before the loop
Add the line to the list

demo.src:

while len(name) > 0:
    member = member + [name]
    name = f.readline()

cards.t: Searching strings: find()
cards.en:
Intuition: like Ctrl+F. It tells you where the word first appears.

Rule: the_string.find(target)

  • Found → returns the index of the first occurrence (index starts at 0).
  • Not found → returns -1.
  • Optional 2nd parameter = start index: find("is", 3).
  • Case-sensitive: "IS" ≠ "is".

Exam wording: “find() returns the index of the first occurrence of the target string; it returns -1 if the target is not found.”
cards.zh:
直觉：像 Ctrl+F，告诉你词语第一次出现在哪里。

规则：the_string.find(target)

  • 找到 → 返回第一次出现的索引（从 0 起）。
  • 找不到 → 返回 -1。
  • 第 2 个参数是开始索引：find("is", 3)。
  • 区分大小写。

考试写法：“find() returns the index of the first occurrence of the target string; it returns -1 if the target is not found.”

ex.q: s = "banana". Find s.find("an") and s.find("an", 2).
ex.a:
1. "an" first at index 1 (b=0, a=1).
2. From index 2: next "an" at 3.

ex.q: Write an if statement that prints "Found" when "pen" is in line.
ex.a:
if line.find("pen") != -1:
    print("Found")
ex.az: find 不等于 -1 就是找到。

ex.q: A student writes if s.find("T"): to test if "T" is in "Tom". It says not found. Why?
ex.a: find returns 0 (index of T), and 0 counts as False. Not found is -1, which counts as True! Always compare: != -1.
ex.az: 返回 0 被当成 False；应写 != -1。

code.src:
s = "This is a string"
print(s.find("is"))
print(s.find("is", 3))
print(s.find("IS"))
print(s.find("T"))

demo.src:
s = "This is a string"
print(s.find("is"))
print(s.find("is", 3))
print(s.find("IS"))
print(s.find("T"))

cards.t: Splitting strings: split() with whitespace
cards.tz: 分割字符串：split() 以空白分隔
cards.en:
Intuition: cut a sentence into words at the gaps.

Rule: the_string.split()

  • Splits using whitespace (space, tab, \n) as the default delimiter (separator) and returns a list.
  • Several spaces in a row count as one; spaces at the ends are ignored.
  • len(s.split()) counts words.
  • The original string is unchanged.

Exam wording: “split() splits the string into list items using whitespace as the delimiter and returns the list.”
cards.zh:
直觉：在空隙处把句子切成一个个词。

规则：the_string.split()

  • 以空白（空格、tab、\n）作默认定界符号（delimiter），返回列表。
  • 连续空格当一个；两端空格忽略。
  • len(s.split()) 可数词数。
  • 原字符串不变。

考试写法：“split() splits the string into list items using whitespace as the delimiter and returns the list.”

ex.q: What is "I am fine".split()?
ex.a: ['I', 'am', 'fine'], a list of 3 items.

ex.q: Write code to count the words in essay.txt.
ex.a:
f = open("essay.txt", "r")
print(len(f.read().split()))
f.close()
split() with no argument also splits at \n.
ex.az: read() 后 split() 再 len()。

ex.q: Compare "a  b".split() and "a  b".split(" "). A student says both give ['a','b'].
ex.a: split() → ['a', 'b']. split(" ") → ['a', '', 'b']: with an explicit delimiter, empty items are kept. They are not the same.
ex.az: 指定 " " 时会保留空项，结果不同。

code.src:
s = "  I am   fine\tthanks \n"
words = s.split()
print(words)
print(len(words))
print(repr(s[:6]))

notes.t: No argument: split on any whitespace
notes.tz: 无参数：按任何空白分割

demo.src:
s = "  I am   fine\tthanks \n"
words = s.split()
print(words)
print(len(words))
print(repr(s[:6]))

cards.t: Splitting with a specified delimiter
cards.en:
Intuition: you choose where to cut: at every comma, semicolon or #.

Rule: s.split("#")

  • A delimiter is a character that separates fields, e.g. , (CSV), ; (phonebook), #, /.
  • Empty items are kept: "a,,b".split(",") → ['a', '', 'b'].
  • Number of items = delimiters + 1.
  • Splits can be chained with indexes.

Exam wording: “split(delimiter) splits the string at each delimiter and returns a list of the fields.”
cards.zh:
直觉：由你决定在哪里切：逗号、分号或 #。

规则：s.split("#")

  • 定界符号（delimiter）是分隔字段的字符，如 ,、;、#、/。
  • 空项保留。
  • 项数 = 分隔符数 + 1。
  • 可以连续分割并用索引取值。

考试写法：“split(delimiter) splits the string at each delimiter and returns a list of the fields.”

ex.q: Give "Gary;Lee;Home;23546030".split(";")[3].
Get the year from d = "25/12/2026".
ex.a: d.split("/")[2] → "2026" (a string; use int() for maths).

ex.q: A student uses int("apple,1,946".split(",")[2]) + 1 but wrote split(";") by mistake. What happens?
ex.a: With ";" there is no delimiter in the string, so the list has only 1 item; index [2] gives IndexError. Use the file's real delimiter ",".
ex.az: 分隔符用错，只有 1 项，索引 2 出错。

code.src:
s = "cat#dog#bird"
print(s.split("#"))
print("a,,b".split(","))
d = "10/06#Rainy"
print(d.split("#")[0].split("/")[1])
print(len("1;2;3;4".split(";")))

notes.tz: 连续分割：取日期，再取月份

demo.src:

print("a,,b".split(","))
d = "10/06#Rainy"
print(d.split("#")[0].split("/")[1])
print(len("1;2;3;4".split(";")))

cards.t: Replacing strings: replace()
cards.en:
Intuition: “Find and Replace” in Word.

Rule: the_string.replace(old, new)

  • Returns a new string with old changed to new.
  • No count → all occurrences replaced.
  • 3rd parameter = number of replacements, from the left.
  • Replace with "" to delete, e.g. s.replace("\n", "").
  • Old not found → same text returned, no error.

Exam wording: “replace() returns a new string in which the specified string is replaced.”
cards.zh:
直觉：就像 Word 的“查找和替换”。

规则：the_string.replace(old, new)

  • 返回新字符串。
  • 不给次数 → 全部替换。
  • 第 3 个参数 = 替换次数，从左边算。
  • 换成 "" 就是删除，如 s.replace("\n", "")。
  • 找不到 → 返回原样，不出错。

考试写法：“replace() returns a new string in which the specified string is replaced.”

ex.q: Give "banana".replace("a", "o", 2).
ex.a: Replace the first 2 "a" from the left → "bonona".

ex.q: Remove all spaces from t = "9578 4224".
A student writes "aaa".replace("a", "b", 0) expecting "bbb" (0 = all). What is the result?
ex.a: Count 0 means replace 0 times → "aaa". To replace all, leave the count out.
ex.az: 0 表示替换 0 次，结果不变。

code.src:
s = "one two two three three three"
print(s.replace("two", "2"))
print(s.replace("three", "3", 1))
print(repr("Rose\n".replace("\n", "")))
print(s.replace("four", "4") == s)

notes.t: Count 1: only the first from the left

code.out:
one 2 2 three three three
one two two 3 three three
'Rose'
True

demo.src:

print(s.replace("two", "2"))
print(s.replace("three", "3", 1))
print(repr("Rose\n".replace("\n", "")))
print(s.replace("four", "4") == s)

cards.t: Misconception: replace() changes the original string
cards.tz: 误解：replace() 会改变原字符串
cards.en:
Intuition: replace() is like a photocopier: it gives you an edited copy, the original stays the same.

Wrong: replace() changes the_string directly.
Correct: replace() returns the new string; the_string is unchanged.

  • Strings are immutable (cannot be changed in place).
  • Always assign: s = s.replace("\n", "") or fruits[i] = fruits[i].replace("\n", "").
  • split() is the same: it returns a new list.

Exam wording: “replace() returns the new string after the update, while the original string remains unchanged.”
cards.zh:
直觉：replace() 像影印机：给你改过的副本，原本不变。

错误：replace() 直接改变原字符串。
正确：replace() 返回新字符串，原字符串不变。

  • 字符串是不可变的（immutable）。
  • 一定要赋值：s = s.replace("\n", "")。
  • split() 也一样，返回新列表。

考试写法：“replace() returns the new string after the update, while the original string remains unchanged.”

ex.q: After t = "cat"; u = t.replace("c", "b"), give t and u.
ex.a: t = "cat" (unchanged), u = "bat".

ex.q: Fix: for i in range(len(L)): L[i].replace("\n", "")
ex.a:
for i in range(len(L)):
    L[i] = L[i].replace("\n", "")
Store the result back into the list.

ex.q: A student writes line.split(";") then uses line[0] expecting the first name. What does line[0] give?
ex.a: line is still a string, so line[0] is its first character (e.g. "R"). Write fields = line.split(";") then use fields[0].
ex.az: line 仍是字符串，line[0] 只是第一个字符。

code.src:
s = "Rose\n"
s.replace("\n", "")
print(repr(s))
s = s.replace("\n", "")
print(repr(s))

notes.t: A line read from a file

cards.t: CSV files (Comma-Separated Values)
cards.en:
Intuition: a spreadsheet saved as plain text. Rows become lines, columns are split by commas.

Rule: CSV (Comma-Separated Values) stores tabular data in plain text, separating rows by line feed characters and fields by commas.

fruits.csvABC
apple,1,946apple1946
orange,2,457orange2457
  • Opens in spreadsheet software as columns.
  • Python reads it with readlines(), replace(), split(",").
  • Everything read is a string, even numbers.

Exam wording: “CSV stores tabular data in plain text; rows are separated by line feeds and values in different fields are separated by commas.”
cards.zh:
直觉：把试算表存成纯文本。每行是一行，列用逗号分开。

规则：CSV（逗号分隔值）以纯文本存储表格数据，行用换行字符分隔，字段用逗号分隔。

  • 可用试算表软件打开，自动分列。
  • Python 用 readlines()、replace()、split(",") 处理。
  • 读出来的都是字符串，数字也是。

考试写法：“CSV stores tabular data in plain text; rows are separated by line feeds and values in different fields are separated by commas.”

ex.q: Write the CSV line for a record: name Ken, class 5A, mark 78.
ex.a: Ken,5A,78 — fields joined by commas, no spaces needed.

ex.q: A CSV file has 10 lines and 4 fields per line. How many commas are on each line, and how many in total?
ex.a: 4 fields → 3 commas per line; 10 × 3 = 30 in total.

ex.q: A student reads "apple,1,946" and computes fields[1] + fields[2] expecting 947. What does she get?
ex.a: Both are strings, so + joins them: "1946". Convert first: int(fields[1]) + int(fields[2]) = 947.
ex.az: 字符串相加是连接，得 "1946"；要先 int()。

code.src:
f = open("fruits.csv", "w")
f.write("apple,1,946\norange,2,457")
f.close()
f = open("fruits.csv", "r")
for line in f.readlines():
    print(line.replace("\n", "").split(","))
f.close()

notes.tz: 行 → 字段列表（都是字符串）

demo.src:

cards.t: CSV to a 2D list, then convert data types
cards.tz: CSV 转二维列表并转换数据类型
cards.en:
Intuition: turn the text file back into a table you can do maths with.

4 steps (Checkpoint 7.1):

  1. readlines() → list of lines.
  2. replace("\n", "") → remove line feed.
  3. split(",") → each line becomes a list, giving a 2D list (a list of lists). fruits[i][j] = row i, field j.
  4. int() / float() → convert number fields.

Why step 4? As strings, "10" < "9" is True (compared letter by letter).

Exam wording: “Remove the line feed with replace(), split each line by the delimiter into a 2D list, then convert numeric fields with int().”
cards.zh:
直觉：把文本文件变回一张可以计算的表格。

4 步（Checkpoint 7.1）：

  1. readlines() → 行列表。
  2. replace("\n", "") → 删换行。
  3. split(",") → 每行变列表，成为二维列表（2D list）。fruits[i][j] = 第 i 行第 j 个字段。
  4. int()/float() → 转换数字字段。

为何要第 4 步？字符串比较时 "10" < "9" 是 True（逐字比较）。

考试写法：“Remove the line feed with replace(), split each line by the delimiter into a 2D list, then convert numeric fields with int().”

ex.q: After the 4 steps on the sample file, give fruits[1].
ex.a: ['orange', 2, 457] — name stays a string, numbers are int.

ex.q: Write code to find the total of field 2 of all rows.
ex.a:
total = 0
for i in range(0, len(fruits)):
    total = total + fruits[i][2]
print(total)
946 + 457 + 646 = 2049.

ex.q: A student skips step 2. What is fruits[0][2] after split and int()?
ex.a: "946 " … for the last field of non-last lines. int("946 ") actually works (int ignores whitespace), but a string field at the end, e.g. "apple ", keeps the and comparisons fail. Always do step 2.
ex.az: int 可容忍 \n，但文字字段会带着 \n 导致比较失败，所以一定要做第 2 步。

code.src:
f = open("fruits.csv", "w")
f.write("apple,1,946\norange,2,457\ncherry,3,646")
f.close()
f = open("fruits.csv", "r")
fruits = f.readlines()
f.close()
for i in range(0, len(fruits)):
    fruits[i] = fruits[i].replace("\n", "")
    fruits[i] = fruits[i].split(",")
    for j in range(1, 3):
        fruits[i][j] = int(fruits[i][j])
print(fruits)
print(fruits[2][2] + fruits[0][2])

notes.tz: 第 3 步：行变列表（二维列表）

cards.t: String functions vs spreadsheet text functions

PythonSpreadsheetDifference

cards.t: Writing into files: write()
cards.en:
Intuition: print() writes to the screen; write() writes into the file.

Rule: f.write("text")

  • The file must be opened in a writing mode ("w", "a" or "x").
  • "w": new content overwrites old. "a": new content is added to the end.
  • Only accepts a string: f.write(str(total)).
  • "r" mode + write() → error (read-only).
  • Close afterwards so the content is saved.

Exam wording: “If the mode is w, the new content overwrites the old content; if the mode is a, the new content is added to the end of the file.”
cards.zh:
直觉：print() 写到屏幕；write() 写进文件。

规则：f.write("text")

  • 必须用写入模式打开（"w"、"a"、"x"）。
  • "w"：覆盖旧内容；"a"：加到末尾。
  • 只接受字符串：f.write(str(total))。
  • "r" 模式下 write() 会出错。
  • 写完要关闭才保存。

考试写法：“If the mode is w, the new content overwrites the old content; if the mode is a, the new content is added to the end of the file.”

ex.q: Write code that saves the numbers 1 to 3, one per line, into nums.txt.
ex.a:
f = open("nums.txt", "w")
for i in range(1, 4):
    f.write(str(i) + "\n")
f.close()

ex.q: Which mode should a high-score program use to replace the old best score with the new one?
ex.a: "w": the old score should be overwritten, not kept.

ex.q: A student writes f.write(total) where total = 95. What happens?
ex.a: TypeError: write() argument must be str, not int. Use f.write(str(total)).
ex.az: write 只接受字符串，要 str()。

f.close()
print(open("out.txt").read())

cards.t: Misconception: write() adds a new line automatically
cards.en:
Intuition: print() presses Enter for you. write() does not.

Wrong: each write() starts a new line.
Correct: write() writes exactly the string given; it does not add .

  • Lab 7.2: "This is new content." + append "This is additional content." → both on one line.
  • Fix: put before the new content: f.write(" This is additional content.").
  • before (not after) each appended record avoids an empty last line, the style used by add_record() in 7.5.

Exam wording: “write() does not add a line feed automatically; add before the new content to start a new line.”
cards.zh:
直觉：print() 会替你按 Enter，write() 不会。

错误：每次 write() 都会换行。
正确：write() 只写给它的字符串，不会自动加 。

  • Lab 7.2：附加后两句在同一行。
  • 修正：在新内容前面加 。
  • 放前面而不是后面，可避免最后多一个空行，7.5 的 add_record() 就是这样。

考试写法：“write() does not add a line feed automatically; add before the new content to start a new line.”

ex.q: a.txt has "A". After opening with "a" and f.write("B"), what is the content?
ex.a: AB — on one line, no \n added.

ex.q: Rewrite f.write("B") so B appears on line 2.
ex.a: f.write("\nB") → content "A\nB".

ex.q: A student writes each record as f.write(rec + "\n"). Later readlines() gives a last item "". Is that right, and why does it matter?
ex.a: readlines() gives no "" item, but read().split(" ") does give an extra empty last item because the file ends with . Splitting that empty item by ";" gives [''], and record[i][3] raises IndexError. Put before records (except the first) instead.
ex.az: 文件以 \n 结尾时，split("\n") 会多一个空项，后面取字段会出错。

cards.t: ord() and chr(): characters and ASCII codes
cards.tz: ord() 与 chr()：字符和 ASCII 码
cards.en:
Intuition: every character has a number (its ASCII code). Turn letters into numbers, do maths, turn them back.

Rule:

  • ord(c): character → ASCII code (integer).
  • chr(n): ASCII code → character.
  • A = 65 … Z = 90; a = 97 … z = 122; space = 32.
  • Wrap around: if the code goes above 90, subtract 26. Or chr((ord(c) - 65 + X) % 26 + 65).

Exam wording: “ord() returns the ASCII code of a character and chr() converts an ASCII code to the character.”
cards.zh:
直觉：每个字符都有一个编号（ASCII 码）。先变数字，计算，再变回字母。

规则：

  • ord(c)：字符 → ASCII 码。
  • chr(n)：ASCII 码 → 字符。
  • A = 65 … Z = 90；a = 97 … z = 122；空格 = 32。
  • 循环回绕：超过 90 就减 26；或用 chr((ord(c) - 65 + X) % 26 + 65)。

考试写法：“ord() returns the ASCII code of a character and chr() converts an ASCII code to the character.”

ex.q: Find chr(ord("H") + 2).
Shift "W" by 5 with wrap-around.
A student writes chr("A") + 1. What is wrong?
ex.a: chr() needs a number, and you cannot add 1 to a string. Correct: chr(ord("A") + 1) → "B".

if k > 90:
    k = k - 26
print(chr(k))
print(chr((ord("Y") - 65 + 3) % 26 + 65))

cards.t: Checkpoint 7.2: Caesar encryption written to a file
cards.en:
Intuition: a secret code where every letter moves X places down the alphabet.

Rules of this cipher:

  • Each capital letter becomes the Xth letter after it.
  • Spaces stay unchanged.
  • Past Z, wrap back to A (−26).

Steps: ord() → +X → wrap → chr() → join → write() to the file with "w".

Exam wording: “Each letter is replaced by the Xth letter after it; if the ASCII code is greater than 90, subtract 26.”
cards.zh:
直觉：一种密码：每个字母在字母表上往后移 X 位。

规则：

  • 每个大写字母换成后面第 X 个字母。
  • 空格不变。
  • 超过 Z 就回到 A（−26）。

步骤：ord() → +X → 回绕 → chr() → 串接 → 用 "w" write() 到文件。

考试写法：“Each letter is replaced by the Xth letter after it; if the ASCII code is greater than 90, subtract 26.”

ex.q: Encrypt "XYZ" with X = 5.
Encrypt "HELLO WORLD" with X = 7.
ex.a: H→O, E→L, L→S, L→S, O→V, space, W→D, O→V, R→Y, L→S, D→K → "OLSSV DVYSK".

ex.q: A student uses if encoded_char >= 90. What goes wrong when encrypting "W" with X = 3?
ex.a: W(87)+3 = 90 = Z, which is valid, but >= 90 subtracts 26 → 64 = "@". Use > 90.

code.src:
def encode(original_message, X):
    encoded_message = ""
    for i in range(0, len(original_message)):
        encoded_char = ord(original_message[i])
        if original_message[i] != " ":
            encoded_char = encoded_char + X
            if encoded_char > 90:
                encoded_char = encoded_char - 26
        encoded_message = encoded_message + chr(encoded_char)
    return encoded_message

message = input()
f = open("encoded_file.txt", "w")
f.write(encode(message, 3))
f.close()
print(open("encoded_file.txt").read())

notes.t: e.g. IT IS A NICE DAY
notes.tz: 例如 IT IS A NICE DAY

cards.t: Decryption by encrypting again with 26 − X
cards.tz: 用 26 − X 再加密一次来解密
cards.en:
Intuition: walk 26 steps round a circle of 26 letters and you are back where you started.

Rule:

  • Encrypted with X, then shift again by 26 − X: total shift = 26, so every letter returns to itself.
  • So no separate decode function is needed: encode(text, 26 - X).
  • The user must input the same X used for encryption.

Exam wording: “Encrypting the message again with 26 − X completes the cycle of 26 letters and recovers the original message.”
cards.zh:
直觉：26 个字母排成一圈，走 26 步就回到原位。

规则：

  • 用 X 加密后，再移 26 − X：共移 26，每个字母回到原来。
  • 不需另写解密函数：encode(text, 26 - X)。
  • 用户要输入加密时的同一个 X。

考试写法：“Encrypting the message again with 26 − X completes the cycle of 26 letters and recovers the original message.”

ex.q: A message was encrypted with X = 7. What shift decrypts it?
Decrypt "KHOOR" (X = 3) using 26 − X.
A student decrypts with encode(text, -X). Does the given encode() handle it?
ex.a: No. encode() only wraps when the code is above 90. A − 3 = 62 (">") is never fixed. Use 26 − X, which keeps the shift positive.
ex.az: encode() 只处理大于 90 的情况，负数位移会出错；用 26 − X。

code.src:
def encode(m, X):
    r = ""
    for c in m:
        k = ord(c)
        if c != " ":
            k = k + X
            if k > 90:
                k = k - 26
        r = r + chr(k)
    return r

X = int(input())
secret = encode("IT IS A NICE DAY", X)
print(secret)
print(encode(secret, 26 - X))

notes.tz: 加密时用的同一个 X

cards.t: Deleting files: os.remove()
cards.en:
Intuition: throwing the whole file into the bin, not just wiping the page.

Rule:

  • import os, then os.remove("targetfile.txt").
  • Deleting a missing file → run-time error (FileNotFoundError).
  • So check with os.path.exists() first.
  • To empty a file but keep it: open with "w" and close.

Exam wording: “Use os.remove() to delete the file; check whether the file exists before deleting it to avoid a run-time error.”
cards.zh:
直觉：把整个文件扔进垃圾桶，而不只是擦掉内容。

规则：

  • 先 import os，再 os.remove("targetfile.txt")。
  • 删除不存在的文件 → 运行时错误。
  • 所以要先用 os.path.exists() 检查。
  • 只想清空内容：用 "w" 打开再关闭。

考试写法：“Use os.remove() to delete the file; check whether the file exists before deleting it to avoid a run-time error.”

ex.q: Write code to delete temp.txt safely.
ex.a:
import os
if os.path.exists("temp.txt"):
    os.remove("temp.txt")

ex.q: How do you make log.txt empty without deleting it?
ex.a:
f = open("log.txt", "w")
f.close()
"w" erases the content; the file stays.

ex.q: A student writes f = open("a.txt", "r"); os.remove(f). What is wrong?
ex.a: os.remove() needs the file name string, not a file object; also the file should be closed first. Write f.close() then os.remove("a.txt").
ex.az: 要传文件名字符串，且先关闭文件。

cards.t: Text files as a simple database: fields and records
cards.tz: 文本文件作为简单数据库：字段与记录
cards.en:
Intuition: a text file can act like a mini table that stays on disk.

  • External data is independent of the program and does not disappear when the program ends or the computer shuts down (variables in RAM do).
  • Field = a column (one kind of data). Record = a row (one person/item).
  • phonebook.txt: one record per line, fields delimited by a semicolon.
FirstLastTypeNumber
RoseWongMobile95784224
DanielChanMobile90094786
GaryLeeHome23546030
SallyHoMobile68753694

A program can add, search, delete and amend records.

Exam wording: “Each row is a record and each column is a field; data in an external file does not disappear when the program ends.”
cards.zh:
直觉：文本文件可以当作存在磁盘上的小表格。

  • 外部数据独立于程序，程序结束或关机后不会消失（内存中的变量会）。
  • 字段（field） = 一列；记录（record） = 一行。
  • phonebook.txt：每行一条记录，字段用分号分隔。

程序可以新增、搜索、删除、修改记录。

考试写法：“Each row is a record and each column is a field; data in an external file does not disappear when the program ends.”

ex.q: How many records and fields does phonebook.txt have?
ex.a: 4 records (lines), 4 fields each (first, last, type, number).

ex.q: Write the line for a new record: Amy Lam, Home, 21234567.
ex.a: Amy;Lam;Home;21234567

ex.q: A student stores phone numbers in the file as "9578 4224" with a space, and the delimiter is a space. What problem appears?
ex.a: The space inside the number is read as a delimiter, so the record splits into 5 fields. A delimiter must never appear inside the data; that is why ";" is used.
ex.az: 数据中出现分隔符会多分一个字段。

f.close()
f = open("phonebook.txt", "r")
for line in f.readlines():

cards.t: A. Loading records into a 2D list: load_record()
cards.tz: A. 载入记录到二维列表：load_record()
cards.en:
Intuition: copy the file into memory as a table so the program can work on it.

Steps:

  1. Open with "r", readlines().
  2. For each line: replace("\n", ""), then split(";").
  3. Close.
  • global record lets the other sub-programs use the same list.
  • record[i][j] = record i, field j. e.g. record[2][3] = "23546030".
  • All values are strings.

Exam wording: “Load the records into a two-dimensional list; record[i][j] is field j of record i.”
cards.zh:
直觉：把文件复制到内存成为表格，方便程序处理。

步骤：

  1. 用 "r" 打开，readlines()。
  2. 每行 replace("\n", "") 再 split(";")。
  3. 关闭。
  • global record 让其他子程序共用这个列表。
  • record[i][j] = 第 i 条记录第 j 个字段。
  • 所有值都是字符串。

考试写法：“Load the records into a two-dimensional list; record[i][j] is field j of record i.”

ex.q: Give record[1][0] and record[3][2].
ex.a: record[1][0] = "Daniel"; record[3][2] = "Mobile".

ex.q: Write one line to print Sally's last name.
ex.a: print(record[3][1]) → Ho.

ex.q: A student removes the line global record. Other functions then say record is not defined. Why?
ex.a: Without global, record is a local variable of load_record() and disappears when it returns. global makes it a global variable shared by all sub-programs.
ex.az: 没有 global，record 只是局部变量。

cards.t: Printing records as a table: print_record() and \t
cards.tz: 以表格打印记录：print_record() 与 \t
cards.en:
Intuition: line the columns up neatly, like pressing Tab in Word.

Rule:

  • Outer loop: each record. Inner loop: the 4 fields of that record.
  • print(x, end = "\t") prints a tab character instead of a new line. A tab moves the cursor to the next tab stop, so columns line up.
  • After the inner loop, print("") starts a new line.

Exam wording: “end = "\t" prints a tab character so that the fields of one record are on the same line, aligned in columns.”
cards.zh:
直觉：像在 Word 按 Tab，把各列对齐。

规则：

  • 外层循环：每条记录；内层：4 个字段。
  • print(x, end = "\t") 打印制表符（tab）而不是换行，光标跳到下一个 tab 位置，列就对齐。
  • 内层循环后 print("") 换行。

考试写法：“end = "\t" prints a tab character so that the fields of one record are on the same line, aligned in columns.”

ex.q: How many times does the inner print() run for 4 records?
ex.a: 4 records × 4 fields = 16 times (plus 4 print("")).

ex.q: Change print_record() to show only first name and number.

ex.az: 每个字段一行，表格乱掉。

cards.t: B. Searching records: linear search
cards.tz: B. 搜索记录：线性搜索
cards.en:
Intuition: look through the phonebook from the top, one name at a time.

Rule (linear search):

  • Check record 0, 1, 2, … in order.
  • Match → return the row number (ends the function at once).
  • No match after the loop → return -1.
  • return -1 must be outside the loop.
  • The comparison is exact and case-sensitive.

Exam wording: “If the name exists, the function returns the row number of the record; otherwise it returns -1.”
cards.zh:
直觉：从电话簿最上面开始，一个一个名字地找。

规则（线性搜索 linear search）：

  • 依次检查第 0、1、2…条。
  • 匹配 → 返回行号（函数立即结束）。
  • 循环完都没有 → 返回 -1。
  • return -1 必须在循环外。
  • 比较完全相同且区分大小写。

考试写法：“If the name exists, the function returns the row number of the record; otherwise it returns -1.”

ex.q: How many comparisons to find "Sally"? To decide "Tom" is missing?
ex.a: Sally is row 3 → 4 comparisons. Tom → all 4 records checked, then -1.

        if record[i][3] == number:

ex.a: Record 0 is Rose ≠ Gary, so it returns -1 immediately without checking the rest. -1 must be returned only after the loop.
ex.az: 第一条不匹配就返回 -1，错误。

cards.t: C. Deleting records by marking
cards.tz: C. 以标记方式删除记录
cards.en:
Intuition: cross a name out instead of tearing the page, so the other line numbers stay the same.

Steps:

  1. Reuse the search sub-program to find the row.
  2. If row != -1, replace every field with "---".
  • The row stays in the list: a logical deletion (marked, not removed).
  • The change is only in memory until update_file() writes it back.

Exam wording: “All fields of the record are replaced by "---" to indicate that the record has been deleted.”
cards.zh:
直觉：把名字划掉而不是撕掉那一页，其他行号就不变。

步骤：

  1. 重用搜索子程序找出行号。
  2. 若 row != -1，把每个字段换成 "---"。
  • 该行仍在列表中：逻辑删除（logical deletion）。
  • 改动只在内存，要 update_file() 才写回文件。

考试写法：“All fields of the record are replaced by "---" to indicate that the record has been deleted.”

ex.q: After deleting "Rose", give record[0] and search_recordByFirstname("Daniel").
Give ONE advantage of marking with "---" instead of removing the row.
ex.a: Row numbers of the other records do not change, so saved row numbers stay correct (and the deletion can be undone).

ex.q: A student deletes "Tom" (not in the list) without the if row != -1 check. What happens?
ex.a: row = -1, and record[-1] is the last record (Sally), so Sally is wrongly deleted! The check is needed.
ex.az: record[-1] 是最后一条，会错删 Sally。

cards.t: D. Updating the text file: update_file()
cards.en:
Intuition: after editing the table in memory, copy it all back onto the paper.

Rule:

  • Open with "w" (overwrite) — the whole file is rewritten.
  • Write every record in the same format: fields joined by ;.
  • Write \n between records but not after the last one (if i < len(record)-1), so the file keeps the original format.

Exam wording: “The file is opened in w mode and all records in the 2D list are written back, separated by line feeds.”
cards.zh:
直觉：在内存改好表格后，整张抄回纸上。

规则：

  • 用 "w" 打开（覆盖），整个文件重写。
  • 以相同格式写回：字段用 ; 连接。
  • 记录之间写 \n，最后一条后面不写（if i < len(record)-1），保持原格式。

考试写法：“The file is opened in w mode and all records in the 2D list are written back, separated by line feeds.”

ex.q: Why is mode "w" used and not "a"?
ex.a: The whole list (with changes) is written again. "a" would add a second copy after the old data; "w" replaces it.
ex.az: "a" 会多一份副本；"w" 才是替换。

ex.q: Rewrite the write line using join().
ex.a: f.write(";".join(record[i])) — same result.

ex.q: A student removes the if i < len(record)-1 and always writes \n. What happens next time load_record() runs?
ex.a: readlines() is still fine, but the file now ends with \n; after add_record() writes "\n"+new, there is an empty line before it, which loads as [''] and makes print_record() crash (IndexError).
ex.az: 文件末尾多 \n，之后新增会出现空行，载入后出错。

cards.t: E. Adding records: add_record()

Intuition: write a new name at the bottom of the list.

Rule:

  • Open in append mode "a".
  • Write "\n" first, then the fields joined by ";", so it starts on a new line.
  • The record goes directly into the file, so the 2D list in memory is not updated → call load_record() again.

规则：

  • 先写 "\n"，再写以 ";" 连接的字段。
  • 记录直接写入文件，内存中的二维列表没有更新 → 要再调用 load_record()。

cards.t: Overall flow for updating records
cards.en:
Intuition: take the table out, edit it, put it back.

  1. load_record(): file → 2D list.
  2. search: find the row.
  3. amend / delete in the list, e.g. record[row][3] = "91234567".
  4. update_file(): list → file (mode "w").
  • Adding: write straight to the file with "a" (then reload), or append to the list and call update_file().
  • Numbers stored as text: int() before maths, str() before writing.

Exam wording: “Load the records into a 2D list, search for the record, update the list, then write all records back to the file.”
cards.zh:
直觉：把表格拿出来，改好，再放回去。

  1. load_record()：文件 → 二维列表。
  2. 搜索：找行号。
  3. 在列表中修改/删除，例如 record[row][3] = "91234567"。
  4. update_file()：列表 → 文件（"w"）。
  • 新增：直接用 "a" 写入文件（再重新载入），或加到列表后 update_file()。
  • 以文字存的数字：计算前 int()，写入前 str()。

考试写法：“Load the records into a 2D list, search for the record, update the list, then write all records back to the file.”

ex.q: Put in order: update_file, search, load_record, amend.
ex.a: load_record → search → amend → update_file.
ex.az: 载入 → 搜索 → 修改 → 写回。

ex.q: A stock file has field 2 = quantity (text). Write code to add 5 to record row's quantity.

ex.az: 先 int 计算，再 str 存回。

ex.q: A student amends record[row][3] but forgets update_file(). After restarting, the old number is back. Why?
ex.a: The change was only in the 2D list in RAM, which is lost when the program ends. update_file() must write it to the file.
ex.az: 只改了内存，没写回文件。

cards.t: Glossary and chapter summary
cards.en:
Key terms

  • stream 串流: file content as a continuous row of characters, read by a hidden pointer.
  • Line Feed (LF) 換行: "\n", at the end of every line.
  • End Of File (EOF) 檔尾: marks the end of the file.
  • delimiter 定界符號: separates fields, e.g. , ; #.
  • database 數據庫, field 欄位 (column), record 記錄 (row).

Functions: open(name, mode), close(), os.path.exists(), os.remove(), read(), readline(), readlines(), write(), find(), split(), replace(), ord(), chr().

Exam wording: “A delimiter is a character used to separate the fields in a record.”
cards.zh:
关键术语

  • stream 串流：文件内容是一串连续字符，由隐藏指针读取。
  • Line Feed (LF) 换行："\n"，在每行末尾。
  • End Of File (EOF) 档尾：标示文件结束。
  • delimiter 定界符号：分隔字段，如 , ; #。
  • database 数据库，field 字段（列），record 记录（行）。

函数：open(name, mode)、close()、os.path.exists()、os.remove()、read()、readline()、readlines()、write()、find()、split()、replace()、ord()、chr()。

考试写法：“A delimiter is a character used to separate the fields in a record.”

ex.q: Name the delimiter in "10/06#Rainy" that separates date and weather.
ex.a: # separates date and weather; / separates day and month.

ex.q: Match: (i) a row, (ii) a column, (iii) "\n".
ex.a: (i) record, (ii) field, (iii) line feed (LF).

ex.q: A student says EOF is a character you can find with s.find("EOF"). Correct this.
ex.a: EOF is a marker of the end of the file, not the letters E-O-F in the text. Python detects it when a read returns "". s.find("EOF") only finds the word.
ex.az: EOF 不是文字 "EOF"，读到 "" 就是到了 EOF。

mc.q: Which mode should be used to open a file for reading?
mc.e: "r" opens the file to read its content.

mc.q: Which mode causes a run-time error if the file already exists?
mc.e: "x" creates a new file and fails if it already exists.
mc.ez: "x" 用于创建文件，已存在会出错。

mc.q: Which mode causes a run-time error if the file does NOT exist?
mc.e: Only "r" needs the file to exist; w, a and x create it.
mc.ez: 只有 "r" 要求文件已存在。

mc.q: A file opened with "w" already has content. What happens to the old content when new content is written?
o: It is kept and the new content is added at the end
It is kept and the new content is added at the start
mc.e: "w" overwrites the content.

mc.q: What does os.path.exists("a.txt") return?
o: The number of lines in a.txt
mc.e: It returns True if the file/path exists, otherwise False.

mc.q: Which statement must come before os.path.exists() can be used?
mc.e: exists() is in the os library.

mc.q: What is the data type returned by f.readlines()?
mc.e: readlines() returns a list of line strings.

t.txt has 3 lines: "This is line one." / "This is line two." / "This is line three." (no line feed after line three). What is printed?
f = open("t.txt", "r")
content = f.read()
f.close()
print(type(content))
mc.e: read() returns the whole content as one string.

t.txt has 3 lines: "This is line one." / "This is line two." / "This is line three." (no line feed after line three). What is printed?

f.close()
print(len(lines))
mc.e: readlines() returns one item per line; the file has 3 lines.

mc.q:
t.txt has 3 lines: "This is line one." / "This is line two." / "This is line three." (no line feed after line three). What is printed?

f.close()
print(repr(line))

mc.ez: 第一次 readline() 返回第一行（含 \n）。

mc.q:
t.txt has 3 lines: "This is line one." / "This is line two." / "This is line three." (no line feed after line three). What is printed?
f = open("t.txt", "r")
for i in range(3):

line = f.readline()
f.close()
print(repr(line))
mc.e: After 3 lines, the pointer is at EOF, so the 4th readline() returns an empty string.
mc.ez: 第 4 次读到 EOF，返回空字符串。

mc.q:
t.txt has 3 lines: "This is line one." / "This is line two." / "This is line three." (no line feed after line three). What is printed?
f = open("t.txt", "r")
f.readline()
f.readline()
line = f.readline()
f.close()
print(repr(line))

f.readline()
rest = f.readlines()
f.close()
print(rest)
o: ['This is line two.\n', 'This is line three.']
mc.e: readline() moved the pointer past line one; readlines() reads the rest.
mc.ez: 指针已过第一行，readlines() 读剩下的。

t.txt has 3 lines: "This is line one." / "This is line two." / "This is line three." (no line feed after line three). What is printed?
f = open("t.txt", "r")
all_text = f.read()
rest = f.readlines()
f.close()
print(len(rest))
mc.e: read() moved the pointer to EOF, so readlines() returns an empty list.
mc.ez: read() 后已到 EOF，返回空列表。

mc.q: Which character is stored at the end of every line (except usually the last) in a text file?
mc.e: The Line Feed character \n marks the end of a line.

mc.q: Which statement about the hidden pointer is correct?
o: It points to the last character when the file is opened
It always returns to the first character after each read
It is only used by read()
Each read starts from where the pointer last stopped
mc.e: Reading continues from the pointer's last position.

mc.q: In Example 7.1's loop, which condition correctly stops reading at the end of the file?
mc.e: readline() returns "" only at EOF.

mc.q: A file f has 5 lines including one blank line in the middle. How many items does the readline() while loop (len(name) > 0) collect?
mc.e: A blank line is "\n" (length 1), so the loop continues; all 5 lines are collected.

f = open("ghost.txt", "r")

It should be called after file operations
mc.e: close() does not delete; os.remove() deletes.

mc.q: A file is opened with "r" and the program calls f.write("Hi"). What happens?

Hi is added at the end
